llm.summary: The skill's stated P2P messaging purpose fits much of the code, but the package contains workspace/memory files and hardcoded secrets, inconsistent metadata, and installation instructions that perform elevated remote actions — review carefully before using.

dimensions.detail: The skill name/description (Agent P2P messaging/Portal) aligns with many code files (local bridge, send.py, vps portal, auto_install/deploy scripts). However the bundle also contains unrelated workspace artifacts (MEMORY.md, AGENTS.md, TOOLS.md, user-specific data) and hardcoded third‑party credentials (e.g., a bearer token in TOOLS.md) that do not belong in a generic skill package. Registry metadata (no required env) conflicts with SKILL.md's embedded metadata listing required env vars and binaries.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and AGENTS.md direct the agent to read local config and memory files (~/.openclaw/openclaw.json, ~/.openclaw/gateway.env, memory/*, MEMORY.md, agent-p2p-admin.txt) and to run scripts (auto_install.py, local/start.py, send.py). AGENTS.md even instructs agents to read memory files before doing anything — broad scope creep that can expose sensitive user data. The runtime instructions also SSH to remote VPS and instruct generating/storing admin passwords; those are within deploy purpose but require explicit user consent and careful auditing.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Although the registry listed 'no install spec', SKILL.md and included scripts implement an automatic install: local pip installs, writing ~/.openclaw/gateway.env, and SSHing to a VPS to git-clone a repo, install packages, configure nginx/certbot, create systemd services, and output admin credentials. Executing these remote/root-capable operations without a strict, auditable approval step is high-risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Requested env vars (AGENTP2P_API_KEY, AGENTP2P_HUB_URL, OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL, OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN) are sensible for Portal integration, but the package contains hardcoded secrets and user-specific data (e.g., Tools.md bearer token, MEMORY.md with VPS IP, pem path, sudo password, and example API keys). The code also attempts to auto-read local hooks token from ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json, which is broader access than just using an API key and should be explicitly declared and confirmed by the user.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (good). The skill can be invoked autonomously (disable-model-invocation:false) which is normal, but combined with the install/deploy instructions that perform privileged remote operations and write local configuration, autonomous invocation increases risk—especially if agent behavior or user confirmations are ambiguous. The SKILL.md claims the agent will confirm steps, but many scripts are written to run commands directly.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill implements a full Portal + Bridge deployment and includes many helper scripts — but the package also contains personal workspace files and hardcoded credentials. Before installing: (1) do NOT run auto_install.py or remote deploy scripts until you audit them line-by-line; (2) search the repo for any hardcoded secrets (API keys, bearer tokens, passwords, IPs) and remove them or replace with placeholders; (3) run install/deploy steps manually in a controlled environment (or a throwaway VM) and use a dedicated, limited‑privilege SSH key; (4) verify that the agent will prompt you for each step (don't allow silent autonomous installs); (5) if you want the messaging features but not the deployment automation, prefer to copy only the client/bridge code (local/) and avoid vps/auto_install/deploy scripts; (6) if you lack the ability to audit code, avoid installing — treat this package as untrusted.
llm.findings: [base64-block] unexpected: A base64-block prompt-injection pattern was found in SKILL.md. This is not expected for a straightforward deploy/messaging skill and may indicate embedded encoded payloads or attempt to manipulate agent parsing; it warrants manual review of the SKILL.md and code for obfuscated content.
